1.
By this award, the claim petition bearing MACP No. 782/19, seeking compensation under Sections 166 & 140 of of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, arising out of the accident, would be decided.

2. Briefly stated, the facts as narrated in the FIR and charge-sheet are that on 28.04.2019 at about 06:30 A.M., deceased was returning after completing his official work on a Wagon R bearing Registration No. UP-17J-1830 being driven at moderate speed alongwith his friends namely Rajan and Manoj Kumar.

When they reached near Jandheki Phatak Nanuta, suddenly a Bolero Car bearing Registration No. HR-64-4499 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and at a high speed, came and hit the car of the deceased.
Due to this impact, all of the occupants sustained serious injuries on all over their bodies.
Thereafter, the injured were taken to the Government Hospital by the PCR.
The doctors declared Rahul Kumar and Manoj Kumar as brought dead.
FIR No. 144/19 was registered at PS- Nanauta against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The present claim petition has been filed by legal heirs of deceased Late Sh. Rahul Kumar.

____ _________________________________________________________ 3. Respondent No.1 put in his appearance on 07.01.2020 and on the same date, vakalatnama was filed on behalf of R1 by Ld. Counsel Sh. Kapil Saini.
3 (i) In the Written Statement filed by R1/Driver-cum- Owner, it is stated that on the alleged date of accident, the deceased was driving his car on the wrong side and at a very high speed.
He lost control of his car and wrongly hit the vehicle of R1.
Other general defenses have been taken by respondents.
3(ii) Written Statement was filed by the Insurance Company on 07.01.2020.
Thereafter, on 09.10.2021, application moved under Order VI Rule 17 CPC by R2/Insurer was allowed and amended Written Statement was taken on record.

In the amended written statement filed by R2/Insurer, it is stated that policy issuing office of R2 does not fall within the territorial jurisdiction of this Court and address of R2 for the purpose of service of notices etc. is of Mumbai.
It is further stated that R1 did not have valid and proper driving license at the time of accident.
It is further submitted that neither the deceased nor the respondent are residing or working for gain within the territorial jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court.

It is also stated that the insurance policy was obtained in the name of R1 on the basis of previous policy, which was fake and R2 bona-fide issued the Insurance policy, believing the earlier insurance policy to be genuine and fraud was played upon the insurance company and hence, insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.
Other general defenses have been taken by respondents.

sentences.text: In order to prove the case, petitioners have examined P1 as PW1.

She testified that 28.04.2019 at about 06:30 A.M., deceased was returning after completing his official work by a Wagon-R bearing Registration No. UP-17J-1830 being driven at a moderate speed, alongwith his friends namely Rajan and Manoj Kumar.

When they reached near Jandheki Phatak Nanuta, suddenly a Bolero Car bearing Registration No. HR-64-4499 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and at a high speed, hit the car of the deceased.
Due to this impact, all of the occupants sustained serious injuries on all over their bodies.
Thereafter, the injured were taken to the Government Hospital by the PCR.
The doctors declared Rahul Kumar and Manoj Kumar as brought dead.
FIR No. 144/19 was registered at PS- Nanauta against the driver of the offending vehicle.
There is absolutely no evidence from the respondents to disprove the particulars of the accident or the involvement of the offending vehicle.

The fact of accident involving the vehicle _____________________________________________________________ of R-1,
being driven by R-1 resulting in fatal injuries to the petitioner is not specifically denied or disputed.
The factum of filing of charge-sheet against R-1/driver-cum-owner of offending vehicle is not disputed.

Filing of charge-sheet against driver- cum-owner/ R-1 by the investigating police officer after completion of investigation prima-facie signifies collection of proof of establishment of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle resulting in fatal injuries to the deceased.
IO has been examined as PW2 and deposed regarding investigation and arrest of R1 and preparation of site plan at the instance of injured Rajan on 14.05.2019.
He also deposed that the offending vehicle was caught by the public.

It is seen that there is delay of about three days in registration of FIR and IO has explained the delay by testifying that "No FIR was registered on the same day as the condition of the deseased Rahul was very critical."

So relying upon the testimony of PW1, PW2, and charge-sheet filed on record, there can be no hesitation to arrive at a conclusion regarding rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle resulting into the accident in question.
As far as R-1 is concerned, despite taking up the plea in his written statement that deceased was driving on the wrong side, he has not led any evidence to prove the same.
The site plan placed on record as well as the other documents do no suggest so either.
PW1 has clearly stated regarding the rash and negligent driving by R-1.

sentences.text: If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.

sentences.text: If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:death case Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.

sentences.text: This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand) when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
(iv) In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

LIABILITY 31.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.

As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and,
in this case, insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/violated by insured, therefore, respondent no.2/ insurance company namely Reliance GIC Ltd. becomes liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.
R2 has taken up the plea that earlier insurance policy was fake and hence, R2 has no liability to pay compensation
but I find no merit in such a plea taken by R2.
It is not disputed that the offending vehicle was covered under a policy of insurance issued by R2 in favour of R1/registered owner.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether Rahul Kumar, husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioners No.2 & 3 and son of petitioners No. 4 & 5 died in a motor vehicular accident which happened on 28.04.2019 at 06:30 a.m. near Jandhedi Phatak, Nanauta, Saharanpur, U.P.,
Ritu Raj vs Jishan on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48206802/
2 within the jurisdiction of PS- Nanauta, due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing Regn. No. HR-64-4499 driven by Respondent No.1 /Jishan? OPP ii).
Whether petitioners are entitled to compensation on account of said death, and if yes, to what extent and from whom ?
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v.
Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.
Hon'ble Supreme Court case titled as Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Road and Ors (
2 0 0 9 )

5 3 0 _____________________________________________________________ observed as follows : "15.
There is absolutely no evidence to disprove the particulars of the accident or involvement of the offending vehicle.
Even the factum of accident involving the vehicle resulting in the injuries to the petitioner is not denied or disputed.
PW1 clearly stated that accident occurred due to negligence / rashness on the part of R1.
11.
Thus, prima facie, it is clear that respondent No.1 was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner at the time of accident.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).
13. In New India Assurance Company Ltd. Vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima-facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.
If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.
If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
R1 did not lead any evidence in his defence and it is seen that in the present case, one of the injured namely Sh. Rajan is stated to have survived and though he would have been the best witness to depose regarding the manner of accident, in my considered view, merely failure to examine him before the Tribunal does not adversely affect the case of the claimants, in absence of respondents leading any evidence to disprove the case set up by the claimants.
The post-mortem was conducted on the date of accident itself.
15. Thus, in view of the above, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioners have been able to prove that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into fatal injuries to the deceased victim Sh. Rahul Kumar.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death:
(a) age of the deceased;
(b) income of the deceased; and (c) the number of dependents.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:death case Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and,
in this case, insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/violated by insured, therefore, respondent no.2/ insurance company namely Reliance GIC Ltd. becomes liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, Issue No.1 is decided in favour of petitioners.
In view of the above said judgment, the deceased, who was about 31 years 8 months of age, was entitled to 50% for benefit of future prospects.
As discussed above, one-fourth of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.
26. Thus, the loss of dependency is computed as Rs. 75,90,024/- (35,139 x 3/4 x 150/100 x 12 x 16).
27. In case of Pranay Sethi (supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
In this case, there are four legal heirs of the deceased.
Thus, claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.2,28,000/- (48,000x4+18,000+18,000) under this head.
28. Considering the aforementioned factors, the total compensation is calculated as under:
 S. No. Head Amount  Awarded  1.
Monthly income of deceased (A) Rs.35,139/
 2. Add future prospect (B) @ 50% of 35,139 =
 17,570
3 . Less 1/4th towards personal and living Rs 13,177 = expenses of the deceased (C) 1/4th of 52,709/-
(35,139+17,570)
4.
Monthly loss of dependency (A+B)-C=D Rs.39,532/-
5.
Total loss of dependency (Dx12xE=F) Rs.75,90,144/-
8.
Compensation for funeral expenses (K) Rs.18,000/-
12.
Thus, petitioners i.e. wife, children (two daughters) and mother of the deceased in the instant case, shall be entitled to a total compensation of Rs. 78,19,000/-.
Petitioner(s) in both of the cases shall also be entitled to interest @ 7.5% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Thus, issue is accordingly decided in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents.
R2 has taken up the plea that earlier insurance policy was fake and hence, R2 has no liability to pay compensation
It is not disputed that the offending vehicle was covered under a policy of insurance issued by R2 in favour of R1/registered owner.
In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs. 78,19,000/- (Rs. Seventy Eight Lakhs Nineteen Thousand only) along with interest @ 7.5 % per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realisation except for the period mentioned above, in favour of petitioners and against the respondent no.2.
